## Historical audit — S0028

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r2/fixed_h0/H0/development/commons_105241439/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file’s JSONL lines; all cited observations are complete, not split.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The task was to reconstruct a single indoor RGB image with separate meshes and matching camera and framing. The image itself is not visible in this audit. A classroom is the student’s inferred scene interpretation, not independently verified fact. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | The first program specified wall, floor, two board panels, notice, three desks and three chairs, chalk marks, procedural materials, camera and lights. Furniture assets contained separately positioned tops, legs, braces and backs; chair backs were rotated. These are code-level intentions, not verified connections, poses or visible geometry. Execution failed because desk fillet radius `.028` exceeded half the `.052` thickness; no image resulted. |
| Student response/execution, lines 8–10 | After receiving the traceback in the next request (line 6), the student reduced desk and chair fillet radii and changed a pale-top material branch. The second execution timed out after approximately 600 seconds, with empty output and no image. The trace does not establish whether construction or rendering caused the timeout. |
| Student response/execution, lines 13–15 | The student reduced physical chalk detail, used simpler furniture boxes and changed Cycles from 64 to 24 samples with denoising. The third execution reached world setup but failed because `scene.world` was `None`; no image resulted. The program specified a near-frontal 48 mm camera and two area lights, but their visual adequacy is unknown. |
| Student response, lines 16–18 | After receiving the third traceback and notification of zero executions remaining, the student emitted a complete revision that creates and assigns a world if absent. No execution or validation of that revision is recorded. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher input, teacher detection, diagnosis, proposal, or adoption appears in this student trajectory. The feedback actually received was runner error output, not teacher guidance. The student autonomously made two executed revisions and one further unexecuted revision; recorded student CLI sessions show no tool calls (lines 2, 7, 12, 17). There was no rendered image to inspect despite the repeated comparison prompt.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The observed outcome is **technical and program failure across all three executions**, not an empty patch: the programs contained substantial scene changes. No successful build or formal visual success is recorded. The final correction’s correctness and submission outcome remain unknown. Multiple objects, materials, intended part arrangements and pose are evidenced by code only; reference fidelity, actual mesh connections, occlusion, framing, lighting and rendered appearance cannot be independently checked. A plausible but unresolved hypothesis is that reducing geometry and samples addressed the timeout; the timeout itself does not identify its cause.

**Lessons.** Transferably, execution feedback can expose both geometric API constraints and missing runtime state, while an unexecuted fix remains unvalidated. The particular chalkboard, furniture and material choices are task-specific and cannot be assessed against the unseen photograph.
